title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1 Art & Culture PART-2

questions.question: The first day of the Tamil calendar on 14 April is celebrated as________.
questions.solution:
Puthandu is celebrated as the Tamil New Year, marking the first day of the month Chithirai on the Tamil calendar, which usually falls on April 14. It is observed with the cleaning of houses, wearing new clothes, and preparing Mangai-pachadi, a dish made with varied flavors to symbolize the different experiences of life.

Note: Similar New Year festivals are celebrated across India on this day, such as Vishu in Kerala and Baisakhi in Punjab.

questions.question: Ambubachi Mela (Fair) is held in which of the temples of North-East India?
questions.solution:
The Ambubachi Mela is a major annual Hindu fair held at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam. It celebrates the yearly menstruation course of the goddess Kamakhya.

Additional Info: During this period, the temple remains closed for three days, and it is believed that the Mother Earth becomes fertile during this time.

questions.question: Nag Panchami is celebrated in which month of Hindu Calendar?
questions.solution:
Nag Panchami is a traditional Hindu festival where snakes or serpents are worshipped. It is observed on the fifth day of the bright half of the lunar month of Shravan.

Ritual: Devotees offer milk to snake idols or live snakes to seek protection and blessings for their families.

questions.question: This event is celebrated to mark the resurrection of Christ. Identify the event.
questions.solution:
Easter is a significant Christian festival that celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, which occurred three days after his crucifixion. It follows the 40-day period of fasting and penance known as Lent.

Note: Good Friday marks the crucifixion, while Easter Sunday marks the triumph of life over death.

questions.question: Paramvir Chakra, Ashok Chakra and Vir Chakra are presented during the celebration of which day?
questions.solution:
High-level military decorations such as the Paramvir Chakra (the highest wartime gallantry award), Ashok Chakra, and Vir Chakra are presented by the President of India during the Republic Day parade on January 26.

Context: These awards honor the supreme sacrifice and bravery of the Indian Armed Forces personnel.

questions.question: In which month of the Islamic calendar is ‘Ramadan’,a holy time when Muslims around the world fast and focus their attention on giving to charity (known as Zakat), observed?
questions.solution:
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. It is a period of spiritual reflection, prayer, and Sawm (fasting) from dawn to sunset.

Religious Pillar: It also emphasizes Zakat (obligatory charity), which is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, intended to help the needy.

questions.question: ‘Mati-Akhora’ is associated with which of the following classical dances of India?
questions.solution:
Mati-Akhora refers to the basic 2,000-year-old foundational exercises of the Sattriya classical dance form from Assam. There are approximately 64 such exercises that help dancers achieve body flexibility and posture.

Key Term: These 'ground exercises' are essential for every Sattriya monk or dancer to master before moving to complex choreographies.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam expresses South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideas of _______.
questions.solution:
Bharatanatyam, originating from Tamil Nadu, heavily draws its themes from Shaivism, as well as Vaishnavism and Shaktism. It often depicts stories of Lord Shiva in his form as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance.

Context: The dance was traditionally performed in temples by Devadasis as a form of spiritual offering.

questions.question: Sonal Mansingh, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awardee, is an accomplished dancer of which of the following dances in addition to the Bharatanatyam?
questions.solution:
Sonal Mansingh is a legendary figure in Indian classical dance, acclaimed for her expertise in both Bharatanatyam and Odissi. She has received the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan for her immense contribution to the arts.

Fact: She was the youngest recipient of the Padma Bhushan in 1992.

questions.question: The “Nalacharitam” play is associated with which Indian dance form?
questions.solution:
The Nalacharitam is one of the most popular and aesthetically refined plays in the Kathakali repertoire. Written by Unnayi Variyar, it tells the story of King Nala and Queen Damayanti from the Mahabharata.

Note: Kathakali is a 'story-play' genre from Kerala known for its heavy costumes and elaborate facial makeup.

questions.question: V Satyanarayana Sarma, a Padma Shri awardee, was recognised for which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
V Satyanarayana Sarma, often referred to as Satyam, was a master of the Kuchipudi dance form. He was famous for his Stree-vesham (portraying female characters), particularly the role of Satyabhama.

Legacy: His performances played a vital role in bringing global recognition to Kuchipudi as a classical dance.

questions.question: Kalakshetra style is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The Kalakshetra style is a specific school of Bharatanatyam founded by Rukmini Devi Arundale. It is known for its emphasis on linear beauty, angular movements, and the removal of suggestive elements to make the dance more 'respectable' during the early 20th century.

Note: The Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai remains a premier institute for this style.

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee, Darshana Jhaveri is a __________ dancer of India.
questions.solution:
Darshana Jhaveri is a renowned Manipuri dancer and one of the four famous Jhaveri Sisters. She is credited with preserving and promoting the traditional temple dance forms of Manipur on national and international stages.

Award: She was honored with the Padma Shri in 2002 for her dedication to the Manipuri classical tradition.

questions.question: Nati is a folk dance from which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
Nati is a famous folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, specifically popular in the Kullu, Shimla, and Sirmaur districts. It is often performed during the Kullu Dussehra and is listed in the Guinness World Records as the largest folk dance.

Style: Dancers hold hands and move in a slow, graceful circular motion to the tune of local instruments like Dhol and Karnal.

questions.question: Noted dancer Birju Maharaj bagged the Filmfare award for best Choreographer for which film in 2016?
questions.solution:
The late Pandit Birju Maharaj, a doyen of the Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin gharana of Kathak, won the Filmfare Award for Best Choreography for the song 'Mohe Rang Do Laal' in the film Bajirao Mastani.

Legacy: He was a master of Abhinaya (expression) and footwork, and a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: Who is known as the ‘Father of Modern Dance in India’?
questions.solution:
Uday Shankar is widely regarded as the 'Father of Modern Dance in India'. He was a pioneer who fused Indian classical and folk dance styles with Western theatrical techniques to create a unique 'Indian Ballet' style.

Related Info: He was the elder brother of the sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

questions.question: Khemraj received the Sangeet Natak Akademi award for his contribution to folk music and dance of ‘Kud’. Which state is the folk dance from?
questions.solution:
Kud is a ritualistic folk dance from the mountainous regions of Jammu and Kashmir. It is performed to thank the local deity (Gram Devata) for the protection of cattle and crops.

Features: The dance is performed around a bonfire during the rainy season, accompanied by the Narsingha and Flute.

questions.question: Ishwari Prasad is associated with which of the following Indian classical dances?
questions.solution:
Ishwari Prasad is considered the legendary ancestor and the first known teacher of the Kathak dance form. He is said to have received the art in a dream from Lord Krishna, who instructed him to spread it.

Note: This lineage eventually led to the development of the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak.

questions.question: Ramkrishna Talukdar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for his contribution to the Sattriya dance form. To which state does this dance form belong?
questions.solution:
Sattriya is a classical dance form from the state of Assam. Artists like Ramkrishna Talukdar have been recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi for their efforts in taking this monastery-based dance to a wider audience.

History: It was introduced by the saint Srimanta Sankardev as a medium for Vaishnavite storytelling.

questions.question: ‘Vazhuvoor’is one of the styles of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
Vazhuvoor is one of the distinct styles (banis) of Bharatanatyam. It was popularized by Ramasamy Pillai and is characterized by its grace, feminine movements (lasya), and sculpturesque poses.

Comparison: Other prominent styles of Bharatanatyam include Kalakshetra, Pandanallur, and Mellattur.

questions.question: ‘Luddi’ is a folk dance of which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
Luddi is a celebratory folk dance from Punjab, usually performed by men to mark a victory or a moment of great joy. It involves clicking fingers, clapping, and energetic movements of the body.

Context: While it is popular in both Indian and Pakistani Punjab, it remains a vibrant part of the cultural fabric of Northern India.

questions.question: ‘Ras-Lila’ recognised as one of the classical dance forms of India belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Ras-Lila is the core theme of Manipuri classical dance. It depicts the eternal love of Radha and Krishna and the 'dance of divine love' with the Gopis.

Visuals: In Manipuri Ras-Lila, the female dancers wear a unique stiff umbrella-shaped skirt called the Potloi.

questions.question: Famous dance personality Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which of these dance forms?
questions.solution:
Kelucharan Mohapatra is the iconic guru who is synonymous with the revival of Odissi in the 20th century. He was a master percussionist (of the Pakhawaj) and a brilliant dancer known for his expressive storytelling.

Note: He established the Srjan dance school to train future generations in Odissi.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan awardee, Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, was a renowned guru for which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.solution:
Vempati Chinna Satyam was a renowned teacher and choreographer of Kuchipudi. He is credited with refining the dance form, introducing new solo items, and giving it a more 'classical' structure suitable for the stage.

Contribution: He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai, which trained many famous dancers.

questions.question: Guru Bipin Singh is associated with which of these dance forms?
questions.solution:
Guru Bipin Singh is known as the 'Father of Modern Manipuri Dance'. He was a versatile artist who worked as a director and choreographer, meticulously documenting the Manipuri dance traditions and presenting them in a theatrical format.

Note: He was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966 for his contribution to this dance form.
